issues.description: Recursive flattenRef has no stated invariant or termination proof for the new parent branch
issues.detail: The rewritten flattenRef now has two recursive call sites: flattenRef(ref) at the top and a second flattenRef(seen.parent) when seen.parent !== ref. The original code guaranteed termination by setting seen.ref = null before recursing. The new parent branch has no analogous guard — if seen.parent forms a cycle back through another node's parent chain that has not yet had its ref nulled, this recurses indefinitely. State the invariant ('each node is flattened at most once') and prove termination explicitly, or add a visited-set / second sentinel. As written, this is UNDER-AUDITED with respect to termination.

issues.description: Asymptotically-wrong deep equality via JSON.stringify inside an O(keys) loop, executed for every seen schema
issues.detail: Two new blocks dedupe child properties against parent/def with `JSON.stringify(schema[key]) === JSON.stringify(refSeen.def![key])`. JSON.stringify is O(size of subtree) and is called twice per key, inside flattenRef, which itself is invoked for every entry in ctx.seen. For schemas with large nested objects this is at minimum O(N * K * S) where S is the serialized subtree size — and it allocates two strings per comparison. For a JSON-schema generator this is the hot path. Use structural equality with memoization, or compare by reference where the processor already knows equality holds. Big-O claim of 'linear in seen' does not survive audit.

issues.description: Loop invariant for the 'parent-only properties' deletion is not stated and is fragile
issues.detail: The block `if (isParentRef) { for (const key in schema) ... if (!(key in _cached)) delete schema[key]; }` claims 'child is a refinement — remove parent-only properties'. But `_cached` was captured as `{ ...schema }` before Object.assign merged in refSchema. After the merge-then-restore, `_cached` keys are exactly the child's original keys. The intended invariant — 'after this block, schema contains only the child's own keys plus $ref/allOf' — is plausible but never stated, and the asymmetry with the non-parent branch (where parent properties are kept) is not justified in a comment. A literate-programming-grade comment is required here; the current one-liner is insufficient for code this load-bearing.

issues.description: Test assertion `overrideCount` jumps from 6 to 12 with no explanation
issues.detail: The override() callback in finalize is no longer gated by `!seen.isParent`. The test that previously expected 6 invocations now expects 12 — exactly double. This means user-supplied override callbacks will now fire on parent schemas as well, which is a user-visible behavior change. There is no comment in the test explaining why doubling is correct, and no changelog/release note in the diff. Either restore the gating, or document the contract change explicitly. As-is, this silently breaks the documented 'do not run on references' guarantee that the test name still asserts.

issues.description: Order-of-operations change in process() is not justified by comment
issues.detail: Previously: if parent existed, recurse on parent first and skip the local processor. Now: always run the local processor first, then recurse on parent. This changes the order in which ctx.seen entries are populated and may change which processor 'wins' when both write to the same key. The reversed iteration in the final loop (`[...ctx.seen.entries()].reverse()`) interacts with this ordering. The reasoning ('Track parent separately from processor ref') is stated, but the consequence for traversal order and idempotence of processors is not. A two-sentence explanation of the new invariant would prevent the next maintainer from regressing it.

issues.description: fileProcessor change is correct but loses the per-branch type info silently
issues.detail: The new shape moves shared properties (type, format, contentEncoding, minLength, maxLength) to the root and leaves `anyOf` branches containing only `contentMediaType`. JSON Schema validators that interpret anyOf branches in isolation will see branches with no `type: string` constraint. Most validators merge constraints with the root, so this is technically fine for draft 2020-12; but a literate comment stating *which spec semantics this relies on* is missing. Older drafts (07/04) and OpenAPI 3.0 may not behave identically — and this codebase explicitly handles those targets in flattenRef.

issues.description: play.ts converted to a debug scratchpad and committed
issues.detail: play.ts now imports from a relative source path and contains console.log debugging for the metadata-order bug. This is fine as a personal scratchpad but should not be part of a PR that ships to users; either revert it or move to a tests/ directory with proper assertions.

issues.description: Type narrowing of `seen.ref` from `T | undefined | null` to `T | null` is a subtle API change
issues.detail: The Seen interface tightened `ref?: $ZodType | undefined | null` to `ref?: $ZodType | null`. With `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`, this prevents explicit assignment of `undefined`. The diff does assign `null` and reads `seen.ref === null` as the sentinel, so behavior is consistent — but downstream consumers (if any read this field) may have a contract change. Worth a one-line note in the interface comment.

review.summary: UNDER-AUDITED with patches of ASYMPTOTICALLY-WRONG and NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT. The PR solves a real metadata-propagation problem and the new test cases are good evidence the feature works, but the rewrite of flattenRef adds a second recursive call site without an explicit termination invariant, and introduces JSON.stringify-based deep equality inside a per-seen-schema loop — a quadratic-in-subtree-size hot path on the JSON-schema generation path. The override-count test doubling from 6 to 12 silently changes a user-visible contract ('do not run on references') and needs either a justification or a revert. The fileProcessor restructure is plausibly correct for draft 2020-12 but lacks the literate comment that distinguishes spec semantics across the targets this file otherwise carefully handles. Before merge: state the loop invariant on flattenRef, replace JSON.stringify equality with a structural compare (or reference equality where available), document the override-firing contract, and revert play.ts.
